##### SUMMARY
Ansible should not wrap lines when tty is absent

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bug Report

##### COMPONENT NAME
ansible/lib/ansible/utils/display.py

##### ANSIBLE VERSION
<!--- Paste verbatim output from "ansible --version" between quotes -->
```paste below
2.10
```

##### STEPS TO REPRODUCE

<!--- Describe exactly how to reproduce the problem, using a minimal test-case -->

<!--- Paste example playbooks or commands between quotes below -->
```bash
ansible-playbook foo.yml 2>&1
# alternative that would wrap stderr to 79 chars when redirecting stdout
ansible-playbook foo.yml >>/dev/null
```
The command above will wrap warning messages at 79 lines, something that would make close to impossible to process the stderr lines. Same happens if output is redirected to a normal file.


##### EXPECTED RESULTS

In absence of a tty, the wrapping should be disabled. Easier to implement is by setting it to `sys.maxsize`.

##### ACTUAL RESULTS
<!--- Describe what actually happened. If possible run with extra verbosity (-vvvv) -->

![](https://sbarnea.com/ss/Screen-Shot-2020-08-26-10-35-26.56.png)

As you can see, even redirecting the stdout to a file produces wrapped stderrors, something that cannot be considered as desired in any case. Yes, redirecting stdout makes stderr wrapped... 🤐

too late for 2.12, but it can make 2.12.1

It just feels like this bug keeps getting stuck with no traction? I can't believe so few are having problems with this? We had to implement some janky sed command to fix the output of an ansible-galaxy command in our tooling. And it still doesn't work reliably.
